newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen opponents said held, asylum refused.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen opponents said held, asylum refused.

text.p: Hundreds of soldiers and supporters of Cambodia's ousted premier have been detained and some embassies have refused asylum to his supporters, despite several killings, foreign sources said on Sunday.

The political killings and other abuses occurred in the aftermath of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's bloody overthrow of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh on July 6 and were continuing, the sources said.
They said that some foreign embassies, including the U.S. and Australian embassies, had been refusing to protect fearful supporters of Ranariddh.

Asked to comment, an official of the U.S. embassy said: "They are not categorically being turned away but there is a balance between helping (Cambodian-American) citizens with political involvement and jeopardising the safety of other Americans."
Officials of the Australian embassy were not immediately available for comment.
Earlier on Sunday, the Sydney-based Sun-Herald newspaper quoted a leaked diplomatic cable from the Australian ambassador to Phnom Penh as saying that Canberra should support Hun Sen.

Describing Hun Sen as a democrat at heart, the cable said supporting Ranariddh would only prolong the fighting in Cambodia, the paper said. A government official in Canberra said the government could not comment on leaked cables.

The foreign sources said at least three high-ranking FUNCINPEC officials had been executed, including Secretary of State for Interior Ho Sok, intelligence officer Chao Sambath and Undersecretary of State for Defence Krouch Yoeum.
Government officials said Ho Sok was executed by enraged soldiers loyal to Hun Sen after being arrested last Monday.

The foreign sources said they feared for the safety of FUNCINPEC soldiers at three main detention sites around the capital who were picked up by patrols during and after two days of fighting in Phnom Penh on July 5 and 6.
Several hundred soldiers were being kept at one of the sites and detainees at another site were receiving no food, they said.
Police at the sites said the soldiers were undergoing "political and psychological re-education", the sources said.
The sources said there were reports of Ranariddh's supporters in the provinces being arrested, detained and beaten for allegedly possessing illegal weapons.
Hun Sen has said his rival's soldiers will be released.

On Friday, the London-based human rights organisation Amnesty International expressed "grave fears" for the safety of hundreds of soldiers and officials of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party in the custody of Hun Sen's forces.

The group said in a letter to Hun Sen that his "assurances to the international community that 'there is no persecution' are simply not borne out by the systematic campaign of arrests, harassment and even killings conducted by your forces in recent days against your political opponents."
The foreign sources said that newspapers which supported FUNCINPEC had shut down out of fear of violent retribution for their criticism of Hun Sen in the past.
On Sunday Hun Sen said Cambodia must hold free and fair elections, but gave no date. He also urged all newspapers, including those critical of him, to resume publishing.
